Inclusion frequencies across folds are reported (Heinze 2018) — evaluation stage.

statement: Complementary-pairs stability selection with B = 50 pairs of random halves, each half's first q variables on the lasso path, threshold tau = 0.6 and q = floor(sqrt((2*tau - 1)*p)) keeps the expected number of falsely selected predictors at or below 1 (Meinshausen & Bühlmann's bound q^2/((2*tau - 1)p), which complementary pairs keep under the same exchangeability assumption).
regime: prediction; numeric or yes/no outcome; selection method = stability
decision: stability-selection constants (B, tau, q)
user_sees: "stability selection with complementary pairs (Shah & Samworth 2013; 50 pairs of halves, threshold 0.6) kept a short reproducible panel"; label 'controls false selections, not prediction error'
claimed_basis: Meinshausen & Bühlmann 2010 Thm 1; Shah & Samworth 2013 (JRSS B 75:55); tau = 'the lower end of Meinshausen & Bühlmann's (0.6, 0.9)' (variable_selection.py:57-59).

For a yes/no outcome the base procedure is least-squares LARS on 0/1 (lasso_first), not a logistic lasso. Selection is per column then lifted to terms (any column kept keeps the term), which can raise false term selections above the column-level bound. The bound needs exchangeability and a better-than-random base procedure, which correlated nutrition predictors may violate.

statement: Under inference with exposures tested one at a time and adjusted for the covariates (the feature-wise family), Benjamini-Hochberg adjusted p-values with discoveries at q < 0.05 hold the false-discovery rate at or below 0.05 across the exposures tested; when nothing passes, m tests at p < 0.05 would give about 0.05m false positives by chance alone.

statement: For a multinomial pure lasso (mix = 1) the coefficients are identified only up to adding one number per feature across classes, and any shift within the interval between minus the feature's two middle coefficients leaves both the probabilities and the penalty unchanged; reporting each feature at the middle of that interval (its coefficients' median set to zero) is an optimum, gives the same coefficients whatever solver or last-bit rounding, and is no worse in fit or penalty.

statement: To describe how a fitted model depends on an input when nutrition predictors are correlated, accumulated local effects (Apley & Zhu 2020) on one grid of the input's observed quantiles (20 intervals, gaps split, no curve where an interval holds fewer than 5 rows) shared by every family are sound and Recommended, whereas partial dependence averages predictions over input combinations the data never hold and is ranked lower.

claimed_basis: Apley & Zhu 2020 (JRSS B 82:1059); Molnar et al. 2022 (LNCS 13200) 'ignoring feature dependencies'; MODEL_FAMILY_CONTRACT C10.
notes: [part id F3-023] acceptance/test_explain.py::test_3a_ale_agrees_with_a_numpy_hand_implementation and ::test_3b_ale_of_a_known_additive_function_is_its_own_shape test implementation, not the correlated-input advantage. statement: For tuning histogram gradient boosting under prediction, the search box learning rate [0.01, 0.3] (log), leaves per tree [4, 128] (log-int), min leaf [2, 200] (log-int), L2 [1e-3, 10] (log), column share per split [0.3, 1], and trees [25, 500] (log-int, only without early stopping) contains the well-performing settings, so a 8–16-point quasi-random search over it plus the defaults finds a near-best configuration.

decision: boosted trees' declared search space

claimed_basis: Each dimension sourced to "Probst, Boulesteix & Bischl 2019"; RECIPES §4.1 says the ranges are "conventions, narrowed from the sources" and asks the prediction reviewer to check them.

statement: For tuning XGBoost under prediction, the search box learning rate [0.01, 0.3] (log), depth [2, 10], min child weight [1, 64] rows-equivalent (log), row share [0.5, 1], column share per tree [0.3, 1], L2 λ [1e-3, 100] (log), rounds [25, 1,000] (only without early stopping), with α=0, tree booster and hist fixed, contains the well-performing settings.

decision: XGBoost's declared search space and fixed settings
user_sees: Tuning line and Settings table as for boosted trees; reason "Its settings are searched inside every training fold, with XGBoost's defaults always among the candidates."
claimed_basis: Probst, Boulesteix & Bischl 2019 (λ 2^[−10, 10]; child weight 2^[0, 7]); Chen & Guestrin 2016 / XGBoost tuning notes; RECIPES §4.1 ("conventions, narrowed").

Linear booster excluded because it "treats missing values as zeros" (RECIPES §2.2) and scale_pos_weight excluded because reweighting goes through the imbalance lever, which recalibrates (RECIPES §2.2, §7.3) — both stated as 'impossible by construction'.

statement: Capping a searched smallest leaf for boosted trees at one twentieth of the tuning plan's units (or plan rows for class outcomes), while leaving the standard leaf of 20 uncapped, keeps the search sound and the same in every fit without materially restricting regularization.
regime: prediction; boosted_trees; searched candidates (n_plan ≥ 300)
decision: upper bound on searched min_samples_leaf
user_sees: None directly; changes which leaf sizes the search can choose (e.g. at n_plan 300 the cap is 15 < the standard 20).
claimed_basis: RECIPES §4.1 ("capped at a twentieth of the plan's units"); WAVE_C6A_PLAN §7 ruling 14 (units not rows); no methods source.
notes: [part id F4-005] SMALL_SAMPLE_STANDARD.md §5 itself flags that below 500 rows the cap sits under the standard's 20 so the search 'cannot regularize through leaf size', and asks the methods review to look. leaf_cap at :86-101. test_leaf_cap_units_and_threads.py tests pin the rule, not its adequacy.

statement: XGBoost's min_child_weight is a sum of hessians, so multiplying a rows-equivalent child weight by the mean hessian at the base score of the fit's own outcome (1 for squared error; p̄(1−p̄) for yes/no; mean over classes of 2p̄ₖ(1−p̄ₖ) for >2 classes, xgboost's softmax hessian being 2p(1−p)) makes the searched value mean approximately that many rows per leaf.
regime: prediction; xgboost; yes/no and multiclass outcomes (regression factor 1)
decision: conversion of searched child weight to xgboost's parameter
user_sees: Search dimension label "how much evidence a split needs, in rows"; the deployed min_child_weight in the Settings table.
claimed_basis: RECIPES §4.1 ("at 5% prevalence an unscaled 64 would demand about 1,350 rows per leaf"); xgboost 3.3 root cover check, amended 2026-10-10; C6A §7 ruling 12.
notes: [part id F4-007] The test checks root cover/n against xgboost's own covers (known truth) for the base-score hessian. The rows-equivalence holds only at the base score; as boosting moves predictions away from p̄, per-row hessians shrink, so a leaf's rows-equivalent drifts — the claim is approximate. Standard candidate uses unscaled 1 (xgboost_family.py:72, :592-597).

statement: The random forest's standard settings — 500 trees, each on a bootstrap of every row, mtry floor(√p) for classes and max(floor(p/3),1) for a number, smallest leaf 10 rows for class probabilities and 5 for a number — are randomForest's/ranger's defaults (a true random forest, unlike scikit-learn's regressor default max_features=1.0, which is bagging), and using 10 as a minimum leaf rather than ranger's minimum node size is a stricter but acceptable departure.

decision: random forest's standard settings
user_sees: Describe: "500 trees, each on a bootstrap draw of the rows; each split tries the square root of the number of columns, and every leaf holds at least 10 rows; the trees' class shares are averaged into probabilities." Quiet term "randomForest's and ranger's defaults".
claimed_basis: Liaw & Wiener 2002 (randomForest); Wright & Ziegler 2017 (ranger); Probst, Wright & Boulesteix 2019; RECIPES §2.2.

decision: forest's declared search space
user_sees: Settings table after the fit (mtry share, sample fraction, minimum node size).

statement: On the pre-fit shelf, boosted trees are the best default for prediction at ≥2,000 training rows (score 3.0, above elastic net 2.5 and forest/ridge/XGBoost 2.0), fair below 500 rows (they overfit easily and their CV score is noisy), poor below 200 rows or when predictors are at least as many as rows (most splits fit noise), and at most fair under inference (no coefficients or intervals).

statement: On the pre-fit shelf, the elastic net is the top prediction family when predictors are at least as many as rows (score 4.0, with the concern that the predictors it keeps will change from sample to sample), scores 2.5 otherwise, is fair (2.0) under inference because penalized coefficients are shrunk and carry no intervals, and below 50 rows carries the concern that inner CV picks the penalty from very few rows.
regime: pre-fit family ranking; regression/yes-no/classes
decision: elastic net's shelf score and concerns
user_sees: Concerns: "{p} predictors for {n} rows: the predictors it keeps will change from sample to sample."; "Penalized coefficients are shrunk and carry no confidence intervals."; "With {n} rows the inner cross-validation picks the penalty from very few rows."

statement: On the pre-fit shelf, least squares/logistic regression scores 1.5 under prediction (dropping to 0.5 'fair' when rows fall short of Riley et al.'s minimum sample size) and 3.0 under inference (lowered when below about two rows per parameter for least squares or ten events per parameter for logistic), has no unique solution when predictors are at least as many as rows (score 0), and for a multiclass outcome is unstable below 10 rows per predictor parameter.

decision: linear family's shelf score and sample-size concerns
user_sees: Concerns: "{p} predictors for {n} rows: least squares has no unique solution."; "{n} rows for {k} predictor parameters: unpenalized estimates will be unstable."; the Riley / rows-per-parameter concerns from sample_size.
claimed_basis: Riley et al. (prediction minimum); Austin & Steyerberg 2015 (≈2 rows per parameter, least squares); Peduzzi 1996 (10 EPV, logistic) — linear.py docstring; multiclass 10 rows/parameter: "no published criterion is computed for it yet" (linear.py:34).
notes: [part id F4-019] The Riley/Austin/Peduzzi criteria are computed in models/sample_size.py (another fork; merge). The multiclass 10-per-parameter rule (ROWS_PER_PREDICTOR) is unsourced. Unit-floor concern for cluster-robust intervals uses inference.min_clusters (outside area A). [Merged F2-029 at turbotab/core/models/sample_size.py:196; its basis: Austin & Steyerberg, J Clin Epidemiol 2015;68:627 (2 SPV); Peduzzi et al. 1996 (EPV 10); 'severe' at half: none stated.; its notes: GEE's assess also applies EPV 10 for binary outcomes (repeated.py:741-746). Conflicts with the mixed model's 10-rows-per-predictor instability concern (repeated.py:643). Vittinghoff & McCulloch 2007 is the usual counterpoint to EPV 10.]

statement: Robust linear (Huber) regression is not offered under inference because statsmodels' RLM takes no weights and gives only i.i.d. covariances, so it cannot provide the design-based, cluster-robust or HC3 intervals inference requires; under prediction it scores 1.5 (ties go to least squares), 0.5 'fair' below Riley's minimum, and 0 when predictors are at least as many as rows.
regime: numeric outcomes only; prediction (offered) vs inference (refused)
decision: Huber's purposes and shelf score
user_sees: Under inference: "Made for prediction only: it gives no intervals for an effect, so it is not offered for inference." Caution: "Made for prediction: it gives no intervals for an effect."
claimed_basis: RECIPES §2.2, §5 (RLM takes no weights; H1–H3 only; cannot meet ruling 6 / DoD interval kinds); V2X_SEAMS row 8.
notes: [part id F4-020] Also huber.py:11-13, :52-55, :170. test_huber_family.py::test_choosing_it_under_inference_is_refused and ::test_its_purposes_are_read_from_the_declaration_never_its_key pin behavior only.

statement: Huber's M-estimator with threshold t = 1.345 (scale re-estimated at each IRLS step as median|r|/0.6745) keeps about 95% of least squares' efficiency under normal errors and more under heavy tails, needing as many rows per predictor as least squares.
regime: prediction; numeric outcome; huber family
decision: Huber's standard threshold and scale
user_sees: Describe: "…(Huber's threshold 1.345 unless set by hand, the scale re-estimated from the median absolute deviation at every step, no penalty)." Prior: "As many rows per predictor as least squares; under normal errors it is 95% as efficient, under heavy tails more."
claimed_basis: Huber 1964; Holland & Welsch 1977 (MAD constant 0.6745, as MASS::rlm).
notes: [part id F4-021] huber.py:174-176 Prior (kind=convention). test_huber_family.py::test_the_fit_is_holland_and_welschs_irls and ::test_the_stack_loss_fit_is_mass_rlms verify the estimator's implementation against independent IRLS and MASS::rlm, not the efficiency claim. statement: Huber's threshold should not be tuned by cross-validation on squared error, because the squared-error primary score would drive the threshold toward no robustness (least squares); it is fixed at 1.345 unless set by hand within [1, 3].
regime: prediction; numeric outcome; huber family
decision: whether Huber's threshold is searched
user_sees: Tuning reason: "Squared error would walk the threshold toward no robustness at all, so it is set, not searched."

notes: [part id F4-022] Also huber.py:15-17, T_RANGE (1, 3) at :56. Implicitly asserts the CV-optimal threshold under squared error drifts upward; true in expectation only when errors make the mean the target.

statement: For ridge under prediction, searching the per-row penalty λ on standardized columns over 50 log-spaced values from 10⁻⁵ to 10² (logistic: C = 1/(nλ) on the same grid) covers the useful range, including the near-zero penalties that can be best on wide data.
regime: prediction; ridge; regression/yes-no/classes
decision: ridge's penalty grid
user_sees: Describe: "Pulls every coefficient toward zero by one penalty, chosen along a path of 50 strengths within the training rows it is given; keeps every predictor."
claimed_basis: Probst, Boulesteix & Bischl 2019 (glmnet gained most from tuning); Kobak et al. 2020 (best penalty on wide data can be near zero); RECIPES §4.1.
notes: [part id F4-024] Grid is in per-row units, so the same λ means the same pull at any n (ridge.py:4-12). Kobak et al. also report the optimal penalty can be negative, which the grid cannot reach. Tests (test_path_search.py::test_t2a…) check the closed form, not range adequacy.

statement: For the elastic net under prediction, searching the lasso-ridge mix over (0.1, 0.5, 0.7, 0.9, 0.95, 1) with 100 log-spaced ratios from 1 down to 10⁻³ of each split's own λ_max (classes: mix (0.2, 0.6, 1) × 8 ratios) covers the useful penalties, with the pure-ridge end left to the ridge family and the nearly unpenalized end to the linear family.
regime: prediction; elastic_net (and screened elastic net); regression/yes-no/classes
decision: elastic net's path grid
user_sees: Describe: "Chooses the penalty's strength and its lasso-ridge mix along a path, by an inner cross-validation within the training rows it is given."
claimed_basis: glmnet's λ path (Friedman, Hastie & Tibshirani 2010); Probst, Boulesteix & Bischl 2019; RECIPES §4.1. The logistic grid's coarseness is justified by saga's cost (≈150 s per multiclass fit on 17,000 rows).
notes: [part id F4-025] Comment at elastic_net.py:82-84 says "glmnet's 100 down to 10⁻³ of λ_max"; glmnet's documented default lambda.min.ratio is 1e-4 (n ≥ p) or 0.01 (n < p); 10⁻³ matches scikit-learn's eps. λ_max formula (elastic_net.py:362-376) is checked by test_path_search.py::test_each_split_reads_its_own_lambda_max_and_it_is_where_every_coefficient_leaves (known truth). The 8-point logistic grid is cost-driven, not methods-driven.

decision: inference table type for penalized families

statement: A scaled condition number (Belsley: intercept plus each column scaled to unit length) of 1,000 or more for a linear model's matrix means some columns are close to an exact linear combination of others so their separate coefficients are not identified, and the columns with variance-decomposition proportion ≥ 0.5 on the smallest singular value are the ones involved; one of them should be left out.
regime: linear family; any outcome; after the fit
decision: collinearity concern on the linear model
user_sees: "The model matrix is nearly singular (scaled condition number {k}): {cols} are close to a fixed combination of each other, so their separate coefficients are not identified; leave one of them out."
claimed_basis: Belsley, Kuh & Welsch 1980 ("Above 30 is the usual 'moderate' mark; 1,000 is far past 'strong'").
notes: [part id F4-032] collinearity_concern at linear.py:60-90. 'Not identified' is strong for a large-but-finite condition number (coefficients are identified but imprecise). test_review_fixes.py::test_shares_that_sum_to_one_hundred_make_the_linear_design_nearly_singular is a known-truth fixture (exact composition fires; well-posed design silent) but does not test the 1,000 threshold or the 0.5 proportion rule.

statement: For an ordinal outcome, the proportional-odds model should rank first (3.0 under prediction, 3.5 under inference), and every family that treats the ordered levels as unordered classes should be marked down by 1.0, because a cumulative-link model uses the full ordering and handles ties while a multinomial model, a linear model on the score, or a split does not.

decision: family order for ordinal outcomes
user_sees: Order-blind concern: "Treats the ordered levels as unordered classes, so it ignores their order."; card consequence "Cumulative odds ratios for an ordered outcome, the same at every cut-point; Brant's test checks it."
claimed_basis: CLINICAL_SURVEY_PACK §B6 quoted (ordinal.py:4-6); McCullagh 1980; audit ME-19, RO-10.
notes: [part id F4-034] ORDER_BLIND_COST at base.py:48-49 applied in base.rank (:780-783). acceptance/test_wp12a_ordinal.py::test_2_on_an_ordinal_task_the_proportional_odds_family_ranks_first pins the ranking only.

statement: For a proportional-odds model, fewer than 10 effective rows per predictor — with Whitehead's effective sample size n − Σnₖ³/n² — makes the fit unreliable ('fair'; 'poor' below 5), and a level with fewer than 5 rows leaves its cut-point barely estimated, for which merging it with a neighbor is the usual remedy.
regime: ordinal outcome; proportional_odds family; pre-fit
decision: ordinal shelf concerns

decision: Recommended disposition of the implausible-reporters noticing in the triage (supplement line vs limitation sentence vs act)
user_sees: "Doesn't change your numbers here" with reason "... That is below what would move the estimate; it is checked again after the plan is fixed."
claimed_basis: Calibration: 9 cases (Goldberg plus a ladder of 8 kcal range screens) from 'the dietary proof's simplified pipeline' on the NHANES fixture (complete cases, straight-line nutrients), one band-0 prediction that held (m_pre 0.0012 → m_post 0.011); band_1 lowered from the convention 0.05 to the smallest falsely reassured case; min_cases 5 (convention)
notes: [part id F6-007] Also materiality.py:1261-1310 (calibrate), 1034-1036 (band-0 text), materiality_cases.py. Threshold is fit in-sample to zero false reassurance on the same 9 cases from one table and one simplified pipeline; SURFACING_POLICY §2.6 requires the twelve reference journeys and a cry-wolf budget, neither used (the JSON 'about' admits the journeys are still to come). test_materiality.py::test_the_committed_calibration_reassures_falsely_on_none_of_its_cases is in-sample. Post-lock verify() relabels openly if the realized band is higher, which limits harm.

statement: An outcome-blind proxy instrument's band 0 ('doesn't change your numbers here') is trustworthy once it has at least 5 calibration cases including at least one band-0 prediction that stayed below 0.1 half-width after the lock, with its band-1 threshold lowered to the smallest predicted value of any case that was falsely reassured; short of that the proxy is floored at 'could bias', while an instrument exact by theorem needs no cases.
regime: Every predicted (pre-lock) materiality instrument; Estimate and Describe chiefly
decision: Whether a proxy may silence a noticing or a Confirm line (band 0) or must say could bias
user_sees: Indirect: an uncalibrated proxy's noticing reads "Could bias the estimate" instead of "Doesn't change your numbers here"; the triage item carries calibrated true/false.
claimed_basis: SURFACING_POLICY §2.6 ('the engine may say could bias but never doesn't change your numbers here from an uncalibrated proxy'); materiality_calibration.json min_cases_reason (convention)
notes: [part id F6-008] Also materiality.py:1261-1310 (calibrate), 232-236 (would_change), materiality_calibration.json:12-13. The floor is conservative; the risky half is the release condition (5 cases, 1 held band 0, in-sample threshold, no held-out check). Policy §2.6 says thresholds minimize false reassurance at a cry-wolf budget; calibrate() only lowers band_1 and never uses a budget. test_materiality.py::test_a_proxy_says_below_noise_only_on_enough_cases_and_a_band_zero_that_held pins the rule, not its validity.

statement: After the lock under Estimate or Describe, an alternative that moves the exposure's estimate by less than 0.1 of the primary's 95% interval half-width is below noise ('doesn't change your numbers here'), 0.1 to 0.5 'could bias the estimate', and 0.5 or more 'act on it'; any sign change, or a change in whether the interval excludes no effect, is 'act on it' whatever the size of the move.
regime: Estimate or Describe after the lock; realized instruments (the every-row sensitivity refit, regression calibration's corrected coefficient); the largest move over the exposure's model-matrix columns and families
decision: Realized band and verdict in the materiality ledger; an upgrade relabels the exhibit and drafts a limitation sentence
user_sees: "Checked after the plan was fixed: refitting on every row moved the estimate from 0.05 to 0.062, 0.63 of its interval's half-width."; upgrade label "Moved more than predicted. ... Before the plan was fixed it was expected to possibly bias the estimate."
claimed_basis: SURFACING_POLICY §2.4 starting conventions τ₀ = 0.1, τ₁ = 0.5 (materiality_calibration.json tau_0_reason, tau_1_reason)
notes: [part id F6-009] Also materiality.py:186-201 (band_of), 442-493 (realized_from_sensitivity, realized_from_calibration), 1086-1102 (verify), 1202-1203 (upgrade drafts a limitation), materiality_calibration.json:4-7. The sign-change rule makes a tiny move of a near-zero estimate 'act on it'; the null-crossing rule makes the band depend on significance status. Movement is not scaled for the alternative's own sampling noise (the every-row fit shares most rows with the primary).

statement: When replicate recalls give the exposure's reliability λ (one-way random-effects method of moments: λ = σ²b / (σ²b + σ²w / k̄)), a regression slope on the exposure is attenuated by the factor 1 − λ, so 1 − λ of 0.5 or more is 'act on it' (declare regression calibration) and smaller values 'could bias'.
regime: Dietary lens; repeats recorded as replicates of a person; at least two people with two or more recalls; any model for the outcome, with any adjustment set
decision: Predicted band and triage disposition of the day-to-day-variance noticing (whether to declare regression calibration or draft a limitation)
user_sees: "About 62% of a slope on `sugar` would be lost to day-to-day noise (λ = 0.38)." label "attenuation 1 − λ = 0.620"
claimed_basis: Hutcheon et al. 2010 (regression dilution); SURFACING_POLICY §2.3 item 1; bands 0.2/0.5 are starting conventions
notes: [part id F6-010] Also materiality.py:335-359 (reliability), 736-767 (variance_noticing). 1 − λ is the attenuation for a single error-prone predictor with classical nondifferential error; with adjustment for correlated covariates (energy, other nutrients) the relevant factor is the exposure's reliability conditional on the covariates, typically lower, and error in covariates biases in either direction. λ is computed for the mean of k̄ recalls among people with two or more; the exposure analyzed may be one day or a different k. SURFACING_POLICY §2.3 says 1 − λ < 0.2 is band 0; code floors the uncalibrated instrument at band 1. test_materiality.py::test_reliability_is_the_one_way_random_effects_ratio checks λ's arithmetic only, not the attenuation claim.

statement: With one recall day per person and no second measure, the share of the exposure's spread that is day-to-day noise cannot be measured, and that noise could weaken a slope on the exposure by an unknown amount, so the noticing is 'could bias (not measurable here)' and a limitation sentence is drafted unless regression calibration is declared.
regime: Dietary lens; exposure without replicate recalls (one recall day, or days averaged with no replicate rows)
decision: Triage disposition of the day-to-day-variance noticing and the limitation sentence
user_sees: "How much of `sugar` is day-to-day noise is not measurable here: each person has one recall day and no second measure, so a slope could be weakened by it without a sign."
claimed_basis: SURFACING_POLICY §2.1 (not_measurable is handled as could bias); Hutcheon et al. 2010
notes: [part id F6-011] Also materiality.py:1039-1041 (limitation drafted). 'Weakened' asserts the direction; in a multivariable model with correlated nutrients and energy the bias can go either way. Overlaps F6-010.

statement: For an energy-intake screen (and any finding on columns that a declared sensitivity analysis's rules read), declaring the analysis without the screen (every row, or the other rules alone) beside the primary is a sufficient response, so no limitation sentence is owed; a limitation sentence is owed only when the predicted band is at least 'could bias' and nothing was done.
regime: Estimate or Describe; dietary energy screens and any could-bias finding; before the lock
decision: Whether a limitation sentence is drafted for a could-bias noticing or finding (supplement line instead)
user_sees: "... The every-row analysis is declared beside the primary (Banna et al. 2017). Its result goes in the supplement."
claimed_basis: Banna et al. 2017 (Front Nutr 4:45): 'analyses in the total sample without exclusion of participants should also be conducted and reported'; Nolan's ruling 2026-10-09 (a declared sensitivity analysis or a correction counts as done)
notes: [part id F6-012] Also materiality.py:697-733 (reporters_noticing done), 1003-1011 (finding_done: any declared sensitivity analysis whose rules read one of the finding's columns counts), sweep.py:672-685. Banna recommends reporting both analyses; it does not say that doing so removes the need to discuss the bias. finding_done treats any sensitivity analysis touching the columns as addressing any finding about them, which is broad. Limitation budget of 3 per journey (materiality_calibration.json:10-11) is a reporting convention.

statement: A data finding the detectors rate 'info' changes no reported number, whatever columns it concerns, so the triage recommends 'Doesn't change your numbers here' for it.
regime: Any purpose; non-critical finding with no reparameterizing repair, no repair offered and no route to a question, severity info
decision: Recommended triage disposition of an open finding
user_sees: "Doesn't change your numbers here": "A note about the data: no number rests on it."
claimed_basis: none stated (WAVE_C6A_PLAN §3 row Q-a rule 4: 'A note (info) changes no number')
notes: [part id F6-013] The claim's truth depends on every detector's severity assignment, which is outside this file; a referee should check which detectors emit 'info' on columns the analysis reads.

statement: A column that no reported number reads under the current answers (not the outcome, not a model predictor after left-out columns, not a declared secondary or fixed-effects column, and not named by any answer slot other than those that only describe it) can be read with another unit, code or coding, or carry a non-critical finding, without changing any reported number; another role, by contrast, always changes a number.
regime: Roles and purpose answered; otherwise every column counts as read (strictest case)
decision: Placement of 'what your data settled' readings (Confirm vs For the record) and triage disposition of findings on unread columns
user_sees: For the record: "`col_a` and `col_b` enter no analysis, so how their values are read changes no number."; triage: "It concerns only `col_a`, which no analysis reads."
claimed_basis: none stated (logic of the pipeline: models/pipeline.predictors_from_roles, decisions.left_out)
notes: [part id F6-014] Also sweep.py:273-313 (reading_changes, reading_lines), 556-559 (recommend). Correctness depends on analysis_reads covering every consumer: WHAT_A_COLUMN_IS excludes 'missing' and 'adjustment' (read only through left_out), so a column's blanks driving complete-case row removal, the shelf's input profile, or Explore's levers must be covered elsewhere. Mostly a logic claim rather than a statistical one.

statement: A finding that concerns columns the analysis reads, with no repair, no route to a question and severity above info, could bias the estimate (or under Predict the score) if left as it is, so the triage recommends 'could bias' and drafts a limitation sentence unless a sensitivity analysis on those columns is declared.
regime: Any purpose; non-critical finding on analyzed columns, or on the whole table
decision: Recommended triage disposition and limitation sentence
user_sees: "Could bias the estimate" ("Could bias the score" under Predict): "It concerns `bmi`, which the analysis reads; left as it is, it could bias the estimate."
claimed_basis: WAVE_C6A_PLAN §3 row Q-a rule 4; Nolan's rule 2026-10-09 on limitation sentences; SURFACING_POLICY §2.5
notes: [part id F6-015] Conservative default, not graded by any measured movement (band None, sorted with could bias). Lines 556-562, 672-687.

statement: Open noticings must be given their dispositions before the plan's lock under Estimate and Describe (and under an unanswered purpose), or before the held-out rows open under Predict; a disposition recorded after that point would be chosen with the numbers in view, so the triage is refused and each noticing is decided on its own as made after the estimates or held-out scores were seen.
regime: All purposes; gate = plan lock (Estimate, Describe, unanswered) or seal opened (Predict)
decision: Whether 'Confirm all' on the open-noticings triage is accepted
user_sees: "The open noticings are triaged before the plan is fixed, and that has happened: each is decided on its own now, as made after the estimates were seen."
claimed_basis: calm/FOUNDATION §7; UNDERSTANDING_LAYER §7 ruling 1 as re-ruled 2026-10-09 (module docstring); no literature cited
notes: [part id F6-016] Also sweep.py:461-470 (gate_stage, gate_passed). Under Predict the gate is the seal, not the first cross-validated score, so dispositions chosen after CV scores were seen are accepted as pre-gate; the implicit claim is that this leaves the held-out score honest. test_confirm_sweep.py::test_the_triage_is_confirmed_only_before_its_gate_passes pins behavior.

statement: When the exposure family holds exactly one exposure-role column, the choice of multiplicity method changes no p-value or interval, so the stated multiplicity default moves from the Confirm sweep to For the record.
regime: Estimate or Describe; exactly one column with role exposure
decision: Whether the set_multiplicity default is a Confirm line or For the record
user_sees: For the record: "The family holds one study factor, so there is no other test to account for."
claimed_basis: none stated (the family is every exposure-role column, EstimandSpec.family)
notes: [part id F6-017] A single exposure can still yield several tests (quintile contrasts, spline terms, a declared modifier's interaction tests; sweep.py:473-477 says a withdrawn modifier is 'kept only to count its test'). Referee should check whether the app's multiplicity method ever acts on those; if it does, the line is silenced wrongly. Similar silencing at sweep.py:168-181: no candidate modifier column means the modification default changes nothing (a logic claim).
